clue.text: A grave is disturbed causing unexpected changes

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of their order, so the three words before are to be shuffled

blocks.note: the first six letters of the fodder
the last two letters of the fodder, doing double duty as the verb of the surface

explanation.surface: A desecrated grave sets off a run of strange events, like the opening of a ghost story.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'A grave is', so 'is' belongs to the letters and 'disturbed' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are erratic, unpredictable shifts in behaviour or circumstance, such as the whims of weather or fortune.

clue.text: Valve in vessels raised angle

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts its bottom letter to the top

blocks.note: pots are cooking vessels
to tilt or angle it, as with a hat or head

explanation.surface: A plumbing description: a valve set inside pipework or tanks, mounted at a raised angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 24 across. 'Raised' works as a reversal only because this is a down clue, and 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is the tap on a water pipe used to shut off flow, a type of valve found in most houses.

clue.text: Basic recycled plates

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade in a new form, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen or waste note about plain recycled crockery or metal plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' is the definition as an adjective, as in a staple food.
explanation.definitionFit: Staple as an adjective means chief, standard or fundamental, like staple foods such as rice or bread.

clue.text: Judge has teatime altered to accommodate beginning of sentencing

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
something altered has been changed
to accommodate a guest is to house them

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, seven letters
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A courtroom judge reschedules the afternoon break to fit in the sentencing of a defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'Judge' look like a noun, but it is the verb, and 'sentencing' supplies just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to form an approximate opinion or assessment of a value, size or quantity, which is to judge it.

clue.text: Comrade mixes with men, as appropriate

indicators.note: things that are mixed together are jumbled up, so the letters of both words are combined and scrambled

blocks.note: seven letters of the fodder
the remaining three letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A friendly soldier socialises with the troops, as is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective 'fitting', but it is the verb meaning to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize property for one's own or official use, especially by military authority, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Boat detailed to get container for fruit

blocks.note: a punt, a flat-bottomed river boat, minus its last letter
to net something is to get or catch it

explanation.surface: A boat is assigned the job of fetching a fruit crate.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is a flat boat pushed along with a pole on English rivers. 'Detailed' looks like 'assigned' but means cut off at the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is the small square basket or tray in which British shops sell soft fruit such as strawberries.

clue.text: Odd job man gives fine performance with old tailless mongrel going head over heels

indicators.note: an animal without a tail has lost its end, so the dog word drops its last letter
tumbling head over heels turns something upside down, so the shortened dog word is turned around

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an act is a performance
O is a common abbreviation for old
a mutt is a mongrel; without its final letter it leaves three

explanation.surface: A handyman puts on a good show alongside an ancient dog that does somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: The mutt loses its last T and then flips, giving TUM to finish the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who does all kinds of work, a general handyman taking on miscellaneous tasks.

clue.text: Surly animal crossing river

blocks.note: a moose is a large deer
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered beast wading across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' could be many things; the letter count and the R inside narrow it to the moose.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen, gloomy and ill-humoured, the same sour unfriendly temper as someone surly.

clue.text: Star carrying animal to old Japanese dictator

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it

blocks.note: the Sun is a star
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A celebrity brings a pet along to meet a historical Japanese ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but here it is the Sun, which wraps around the hog.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoguns were hereditary military rulers who governed Japan in the emperor's name until the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Light close to central current unit

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical description of a light fitting near a central power unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the close, or end, of 'central'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives out illumination, so it is a light in the everyday household sense.

clue.text: Late MP ran frantically round independent part of government

indicators.note: done frantically means done in a wild disordered rush, so the letters are thrown into a new order
running round something circles it

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, nine letters
I is the abbreviation for independent, as for a politician without a party

explanation.surface: A tardy politician dashes around an independent member, all within the corridors of power.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface fits the answer; the only trick is spotting the I held inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the legislature, the elected law-making body that forms one branch of a state's governing system.

clue.text: Introduction to timely subject in paper?

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
an issue is a subject or topic under discussion

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead-in to a topical story.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper picture makes 'paper' a publication; the question mark flags that it means thin paper, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is soft, very thin paper, used for wrapping gifts or as a disposable handkerchief.

clue.text: Chap tucked into dish, then returned soldier's portable grill

indicators.note: something tucked into a thing is placed inside it
something returned goes back the way it came, so the soldiers' abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: a salad is a dish
a chap is a man
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A hungry man eats his meal, then goes back to a soldier's camp stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on 'soldier' is the possessive linking to the definition; the wordplay part is just RE. The eating picture makes 'tucked into' look like eating, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a metal plate heated and held over food to brown it, or a small overhead kitchen grill.

clue.text: Stand in part of theatre, including nationally acclaimed trio, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so the first letters of the three words are taken

blocks.note: the stage is where the actors perform
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An understudy fills in at a theatre show starring a famous three-piece act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand in' reads as one phrase meaning deputise, but 'Stand' alone is the definition, in the sense of standing still.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that stands without flowing goes stale; to stagnate is to remain motionless, inactive or undeveloped.

clue.text: Join priest cutting piece of cake?

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another goes into its middle

blocks.note: a slice is a piece of cake
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A vicar is asked to join in slicing the wedding cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A priest and cake summon a wedding, where splicing is slang for marrying, so the surface winks at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to unite two ropes, films or tapes by weaving or fixing their ends together.

clue.text: Animal heard about 22 down

definitions.note: cross-reference to THRONE, whose clue gives 'Bishop's seat'

indicators.note: things turned about are moved around

blocks.note: a cat is an animal
the anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: An animal is heard somewhere around a throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like a sound signal but it is simply anagram fodder. The answer is the throne from which a cathedral takes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedra is a bishop's official chair in the cathedral, the formal throne from which he presides.

clue.text: Man succeeding retired queen as interim ruler

indicators.note: retiring means going back

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man takes over from a queen who has stepped down, ruling for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' is positional: the man comes after the retired queen in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent governs a kingdom temporarily while the monarch is a child, absent or incapacitated.

clue.text: Check for second time in social media platform for one watching birds

indicators.note: one thing put in for another replaces it

blocks.note: Twitter, now renamed X, was the microblogging site
T is the abbreviation for time
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: Someone double-checks something on a social network while bird-spotting.
explanation.walkthrough: The platform has two Ts; 'second' says it is the latter that is swapped out. Twitter's bird logo makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, especially one who travels far to tick off sightings of rare species.

clue.text: Performer in cart is terrific

indicators.note: the answer is inside the run of letters that follows, spanning the word boundaries

blocks.note: running letters across three words

explanation.surface: A travelling entertainer's wagon is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'cart' through 'is' to the first letter of 'terrific'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist can be an entertainer such as a singer, dancer or actor, as in recording or variety artists.

clue.text: Do remote changes to measuring device

indicators.note: making changes to something alters its form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to tinker with a remote control for a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb of the surface but is part of the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is the instrument in a vehicle that records distance travelled, a mileage counter.

clue.text: Writer given one American plant

blocks.note: Roald Dahl, the children's author
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An author receives a houseplant from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' could be anyone; the letter count and the crossings point to Roald Dahl.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a Mexican garden flower grown from tubers, with showy many-petalled blooms.

clue.text: Hand over vessel with metal coating

indicators.note: a coating surrounds what it covers

blocks.note: tin is a metal
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone passes across a tin-plated pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over vessel' reads as one action, but 'Hand over' is the definition and 'vessel' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in something, such as a weapon or a suspect, is to surrender it or give it up to authorities.

clue.text: Bishop's seat moved north-east

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are no longer in their place, so the compass words are rearranged

blocks.note: the word itself, five letters of fodder
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A cathedral's episcopal chair has been relocated to the north-east corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'east' is abbreviated; 'north' stays whole. 'Bishop' is not the chess piece or B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop presides from a ceremonial throne in the cathedral, the chair that symbolises the office.

clue.text: Cleaner hid broken light

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner concealed a lamp they had smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like the definition but is fodder; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandelier is a decorative hanging fitting with branches holding several bulbs or candles, which gives illumination.

clue.text: See 2
Get rid of slight squint

blocks.note: to throw away or discard, as a snake sheds its skin
a mild misalignment of one eye

explanation.surface: Advice to correct a minor eye defect.
explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of the same short word, one a verb, one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast means discard, as snakes cast skins; and a cast in the eye is a slight misalignment or strabismus.

clue.text: One-dimensional retro part of transport infrastructure crossing small space

indicators.note: a track crossing a gap spans it

blocks.note: a rail is part of a railway track
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A dull old-fashioned bit of road or rail cutting through a little plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The rail goes round the en first and the whole is then reversed. An en is a typesetting unit of space, the width of a letter n.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged along a single line, extending in only one direction, as in geometry.

clue.text: Metal cask German sent abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
G is the abbreviation for German
the anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: A metal barrel is shipped overseas by a German exporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' looks like overseas travel but signals the shuffle of 'sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard, dense chemical element, symbol W, used in light-bulb filaments and alloys.
